audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for sending the Twelve, Herod's question, feeding five thousand, Peter confession, passion prediction, cross-following, transfiguration, difficult healing, greatness, outsider in the name, and setting face toward Jerusalem.

verses.restored: Calling together the twelve, he gave them power and authority over all unclean spirits and to heal diseases.

familiar.text: Then he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases.

modern.text: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.

original.text: Συγκαλεσάμενος δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ νόσους θεραπεύειν,

verses.restored: He sent them to proclaim the reign of the Divine and to heal.

familiar.text: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.

modern.text: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἰᾶσθαι ⸂τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς⸃,

verses.restored: He said to them, Take nothing for the way: neither staff, nor bag, nor bread, nor silver, nor two tunics each.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece.

modern.text: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν αἴρετε εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, μήτε ⸀ῥάβδον μήτε πήραν μήτε ἄρτον μήτε ἀργύριον, μήτε ⸀ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας ἔχειν.

verses.restored: Whatever house you enter, remain there, and from there go out.

familiar.text: And whatsoever house ye enter into, there abide, and thence depart.

modern.text: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.

original.text: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν οἰκίαν εἰσέλθητε, ἐκεῖ μένετε καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐξέρχεσθε.

verses.restored: As many as do not receive you, going out from that city, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.

familiar.text: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.

modern.text: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”

original.text: καὶ ὅσοι ⸀ἂν μὴ ⸀δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξερχόμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως ⸀ἐκείνης τὸν κονιορτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ⸀ἀποτινάσσετε εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπʼ αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Going out, they traveled through the villages, announcing good news and healing everywhere.

familiar.text: And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel, and healing every where.

modern.text: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere. Herod Tries to See Jesus (Matthew 14:1–12; Mark 6:14–29)

original.text: ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας εὐαγγελιζόμενοι καὶ θεραπεύοντες πανταχοῦ.

verses.restored: Herod the tetrarch heard all that was happening and was perplexed, because some were saying John had been raised from the dead.

familiar.text: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he was perplexed, because that it was said of some, that John was risen from the dead;

modern.text: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he was perplexed. For some were saying that John had risen from the dead,

original.text: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὰ ⸀γινόμενα πάντα, καὶ διηπόρει διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων ὅτι Ἰωάννης ⸀ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν,

verses.restored: Others said Elijah had appeared, and others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.

familiar.text: And of some, that Elias had appeared; and of others, that one of the old prophets was risen again.

modern.text: others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that a prophet of old had arisen.

original.text: ὑπό τινων δὲ ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐφάνη, ἄλλων δὲ ὅτι προφήτης ⸀τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.

verses.restored: Herod said, John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things? And he sought to see him.

familiar.text: And Herod said, John have I beheaded: but who is this, of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.

modern.text: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus. The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Matthew 14:13–21; Mark 6:30–44; John 6:1–15)

original.text: ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ ⸀ὁ Ἡρῴδης· Ἰωάννην ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα· τίς δέ ἐστιν οὗτος περὶ ⸀οὗ ἀκούω τοιαῦτα; καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: When the apostles returned, they described to him all they had done. Taking them, he withdrew privately to a city called Bethsaida.

familiar.text: And the apostles, when they were returned, told him all that they had done. And he took them, and went aside privately into a desert place belonging to the city called Bethsaida.

modern.text: Then the apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had done. Taking them away privately, He withdrew to a town called Bethsaida.

original.text: Καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες οἱ ἀπόστολοι διηγήσαντο αὐτῷ ὅσα ἐποίησαν. καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ὑπεχώρησεν κατʼ ἰδίαν εἰς ⸂πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά⸃.

verses.restored: But the crowds, knowing, followed him. Receiving them, he spoke to them about the reign of the Divine and healed those needing healing.

familiar.text: And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.

modern.text: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι γνόντες ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ. καὶ ⸀ἀποδεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τοὺς χρείαν ἔχοντας θεραπείας ἰᾶτο.

verses.restored: The day began to decline. The twelve came and said to him, Release the crowd, so they may go into the surrounding villages and farms to lodge and find provisions, because we are here in a deserted place.

familiar.text: And when the day began to wear away, then came the twelve, and said unto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.

modern.text: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”

original.text: Ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤρξατο κλίνειν· προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δώδεκα εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀπόλυσον τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα ⸀πορευθέντες εἰς τὰς κύκλῳ κώμας ⸀καὶ ἀγροὺς καταλύσωσιν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν, ὅτι ὧδε ἐν ἐρήμῳ τόπῳ ἐσμέν.

verses.restored: He said to them, You give them something to eat. They said, We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people.

familiar.text: But he said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more but five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy meat for all this people.

modern.text: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ⸂ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν⸃. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ ⸂ἄρτοι πέντε⸃ καὶ ἰχθύες δύο, εἰ μήτι πορευθέντες ἡμεῖς ἀγοράσωμεν εἰς πάντα τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον βρώματα.

verses.restored: For there were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, Make them recline in groups of about fifty each.

familiar.text: For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit down by fifties in a company.

modern.text: (There were about five thousand men.) He told His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

original.text: ἦσαν γὰρ ὡσεὶ ἄνδρες πεντακισχίλιοι. εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Κατακλίνατε αὐτοὺς κλισίας ⸀ὡσεὶ ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα.

verses.restored: They did so and made them all recline.

familiar.text: And they did so, and made them all sit down.

modern.text: They did so, and everyone was seated.

original.text: καὶ ἐποίησαν οὕτως καὶ ⸀κατέκλιναν ἅπαντας.

verses.restored: Taking the five loaves and two fish, looking up to heaven, he blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.

familiar.text: Then he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.

modern.text: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples to set before the people.

original.text: λαβὼν δὲ τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ κατέκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς ⸀παραθεῖναι τῷ ὄχλῳ.

verses.restored: All ate and were filled, and what remained was taken up: twelve baskets of broken pieces.

familiar.text: And they did eat, and were all filled: and there was taken up of fragments that remained to them twelve baskets.

modern.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over. Peter’s Confession of Christ (Matthew 16:13–20; Mark 8:27–30; John 6:67–71)

original.text: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν πάντες, καὶ ἤρθη τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων κόφινοι δώδεκα.

verses.restored: It happened, as he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he questioned them, saying, Who do the crowds say I am?

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?

modern.text: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν προσευχόμενον κατὰ μόνας συνῆσαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί, καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς λέγων· Τίνα με ⸂οἱ ὄχλοι λέγουσιν⸃ εἶναι;

verses.restored: They answered, John the Baptist; others, Elijah; others, that one of the ancient prophets has risen.

familiar.text: They answering said, John the Baptist; but some say, Elias; and others say, that one of the old prophets is risen again.

modern.text: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, that a prophet of old has arisen.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.

verses.restored: He said to them, But you, who do you say I am? Peter answered, The Messiah of the Divine.

familiar.text: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.

modern.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.” Christ’s Passion Foretold (Matthew 16:21–23; Mark 8:31–33)

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι; ⸂Πέτρος δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς⸃ εἶπεν· Τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: He strictly warned and instructed them to tell this to no one,

familiar.text: And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;

modern.text: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.

original.text: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτοῖς παρήγγειλεν μηδενὶ ⸀λέγειν τοῦτο,

verses.restored: saying, It is necessary for the Son of Humanity to suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and on the third day be raised.

familiar.text: Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.

modern.text: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.” Take Up Your Cross (Matthew 16:24–28; Mark 8:34–38)

original.text: εἰπὼν ὅτι Δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ⸀ἐγερθῆναι.

verses.restored: He said to all, If anyone wants to come after me, let that one deny self, take up one's cross daily, and follow me.

familiar.text: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.

original.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς πάντας· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ⸂ἔρχεσθαι, ἀρνησάσθω⸃ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ ⸂καθʼ ἡμέραν⸃, καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.

verses.restored: For whoever wants to save one's life/soul will lose it, but whoever loses one's life/soul because of me, this one will save it.

familiar.text: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.

modern.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.

original.text: ὃς γὰρ ⸀ἂν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι, ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, οὗτος σώσει αὐτήν.

verses.restored: For what does a person profit, having gained the whole world, but losing or forfeiting oneself?

familiar.text: For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?

modern.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?

original.text: τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος κερδήσας τὸν κόσμον ὅλον ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀπολέσας ἢ ζημιωθείς;

verses.restored: Whoever is ashamed of me and my words, of this one the Son of Humanity will be ashamed when he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy messengers.

familiar.text: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in his Father’s, and of the holy angels.

modern.text: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

original.text: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους, τοῦτον ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων.

verses.restored: Truly I say to you: there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.

modern.text: But I tell you truthfully, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.” The Transfiguration (Matthew 17:1–13; Mark 9:1–13; 2 Peter 1:16–21)

original.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀληθῶς, εἰσίν τινες τῶν ⸀αὐτοῦ ⸀ἑστηκότων οἳ οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: About eight days after these words, he took Peter, John, and James and went up into the mountain to pray.

familiar.text: And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.

modern.text: About eight days after Jesus had said these things, He took with Him Peter, John, and James, and went up on a mountain to pray.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὡσεὶ ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ ⸀καὶ παραλαβὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.

verses.restored: As he was praying, the appearance of his face became different, and his clothing became white, flashing like lightning.

familiar.text: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.

modern.text: And as He was praying, the appearance of His face changed, and His clothes became radiantly white.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ προσεύχεσθαι αὐτὸν τὸ εἶδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ὁ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λευκὸς ἐξαστράπτων.

verses.restored: Look, two men were speaking with him: Moses and Elijah,

familiar.text: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:

modern.text: Suddenly two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with Jesus.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο συνελάλουν αὐτῷ, οἵτινες ἦσαν Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας,

verses.restored: who appeared in glory and spoke of his exodus/departure, which he was about to fulfill in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.

modern.text: They appeared in glory and spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.

original.text: οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ ἔλεγον τὴν ἔξοδον αὐτοῦ ἣν ἤμελλεν πληροῦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.restored: Peter and those with him had been weighed down with sleep; but becoming fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

familiar.text: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.

modern.text: Meanwhile Peter and his companions were overcome by sleep, but when they awoke, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἦσαν βεβαρημένοι ὕπνῳ· διαγρηγορήσαντες δὲ εἶδον τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς δύο ἄνδρας τοὺς συνεστῶτας αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is beautiful/good for us to be here; let us make three tents, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah, not knowing what he was saying.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.

modern.text: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters —one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (He did not know what he was saying.)

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ διαχωρίζεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν ⸀ὁ Πέτρος πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Ἐπιστάτα, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν σκηνὰς τρεῖς, μίαν σοὶ καὶ μίαν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ μίαν Ἠλίᾳ, μὴ εἰδὼς ὃ λέγει.

verses.restored: As he was saying these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them; they feared as they entered the cloud.

familiar.text: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.

modern.text: While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.

original.text: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ἐγένετο νεφέλη καὶ ⸀ἐπεσκίαζεν αὐτούς· ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἐν τῷ ⸂εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς⸃ εἰς τὴν νεφέλην.

verses.restored: A voice came from the cloud, saying, This is my Son, the Chosen One; listen to him.

familiar.text: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.

modern.text: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”

original.text: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ⸀ἐκλελεγμένος, αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε.

verses.restored: When the voice had happened, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and reported to no one in those days anything of what they had seen.

familiar.text: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.

modern.text: After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them. The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen. The Boy with an Evil Spirit (Matthew 17:14–18; Mark 9:14–29)

original.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνὴν ⸀εὑρέθη Ἰησοῦς μόνος. καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσίγησαν καὶ οὐδενὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις οὐδὲν ὧν ἑώρακαν.

verses.restored: On the next day, when they came down from the mountain, a great crowd met him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they were come down from the hill, much people met him.

modern.text: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.

original.text: Ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ κατελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.

verses.restored: Look, a man from the crowd cried out, Teacher, I beg you to look upon my son, because he is my only child.

familiar.text: And, behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son: for he is mine only child.

modern.text: Suddenly a man in the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only child.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ⸀ἐβόησεν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, δέομαί σου ἐπιβλέψαι ἐπὶ τὸν υἱόν μου, ὅτι μονογενής ⸂μοί ἐστιν⸃,

verses.restored: Look, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out; it convulses him with foam and scarcely departs from him, bruising him.

familiar.text: And, lo, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth again, and bruising him hardly departeth from him.

modern.text: A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It keeps mauling him and rarely departs from him.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ πνεῦμα λαμβάνει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξαίφνης κράζει, καὶ σπαράσσει αὐτὸν μετὰ ἀφροῦ καὶ ⸀μόγις ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ συντρῖβον αὐτόν·

verses.restored: I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they were not able.

familiar.text: And I besought thy disciples to cast him out; and they could not.

modern.text: I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”

original.text: καὶ ἐδεήθην τῶν μαθητῶν σου ἵνα ἐκβάλωσιν αὐτό, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν.

verses.restored: Jesus answered, O untrusting and twisted generation, how long shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.

modern.text: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε ἔσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; προσάγαγε ⸂ὧδε τὸν υἱόν σου⸃.

verses.restored: As he was coming, the troubling spirit threw him down and convulsed him. Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the child, and gave him back to his father.

familiar.text: And as he was yet a coming, the devil threw him down, and tare him. And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him again to his father.

modern.text: Even while the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him to the ground in a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father. The Second Prediction of the Passion (Matthew 17:22–23; Mark 9:30–32)

original.text: ἔτι δὲ προσερχομένου αὐτοῦ ἔρρηξεν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ συνεσπάραξεν· ἐπετίμησεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ, καὶ ἰάσατο τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἀπέδωκεν αὐτὸν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: All were struck with wonder at the majesty of the Divine. While all were marveling at all he was doing, he said to his disciples,

familiar.text: And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while they wondered every one at all things which Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,

modern.text: And they were all astonished at the greatness of God. While everyone was marveling at all that Jesus was doing, He said to His disciples,

original.text: ἐξεπλήσσοντο δὲ πάντες ἐπὶ τῇ μεγαλειότητι τοῦ θεοῦ. Πάντων δὲ θαυμαζόντων ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ⸀ἐποίει εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: Place these words in your ears: the Son of Humanity is about to be handed over into human hands.

familiar.text: Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men.

modern.text: “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”

original.text: Θέσθε ὑμεῖς εἰς τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ὁ γὰρ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: But they did not understand this word; it was hidden from them so they would not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him about this word.

familiar.text: But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.

modern.text: But they did not understand this statement. It was veiled from them so that they could not comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it. The Greatest in the Kingdom (Matthew 18:1–5; Mark 9:33–41)

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο, καὶ ἦν παρακεκαλυμμένον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ αἴσθωνται αὐτό, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο ἐρωτῆσαι αὐτὸν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου.

verses.restored: A reasoning entered among them about which of them might be greatest.

familiar.text: Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest.

modern.text: Then an argument started among the disciples as to which of them would be the greatest.

original.text: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ διαλογισμὸς ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς ἂν εἴη μείζων αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their heart, took a child and stood the child beside him,

familiar.text: And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him,

modern.text: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, had a little child stand beside Him.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀εἰδὼς τὸν διαλογισμὸν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενος ⸀παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ παρʼ ἑαυτῷ,

verses.restored: and said to them, Whoever receives this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the One who sent me; for the smaller one among all of you, this one is great.

familiar.text: And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.

modern.text: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ⸀ἂν δέξηται τοῦτο τὸ παιδίον ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὃς ⸁ἂν ἐμὲ δέξηται δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με· ὁ γὰρ μικρότερος ἐν πᾶσιν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχων οὗτός ⸀ἐστιν μέγας.

verses.restored: John answered, Master, we saw someone casting out unclean spirits in your name, and we tried to stop him because he does not follow with us.

familiar.text: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.

modern.text: “Master,” said John, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”

original.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀δὲ Ἰωάννης εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, εἴδομέν τινα ⸀ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ⸀ἐκωλύομεν αὐτὸν ὅτι οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ μεθʼ ἡμῶν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.

modern.text: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied, “for whoever is not against you is for you.” The Samaritans Reject Jesus

original.text: ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ πρὸς αὐτὸν ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ κωλύετε, ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθʼ ⸂ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν⸃ ἐστιν.

verses.restored: It happened, when the days were being fulfilled for his taking up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,

modern.text: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ ⸀πρόσωπον ⸀ἐστήρισεν τοῦ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,

verses.restored: He sent messengers before his face. Going, they entered a Samaritan village to prepare for him.

familiar.text: And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.

modern.text: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ. καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν, ⸀ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: They did not receive him, because his face was going toward Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.

modern.text: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐδέξαντο αὐτόν, ὅτι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.restored: Seeing this, the disciples James and John said, Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?

familiar.text: And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?

modern.text: When the disciples James and John saw this, they asked, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?”

original.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης εἶπαν· Κύριε, θέλεις εἴπωμεν πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι ⸀αὐτούς;

verses.restored: But turning, he rebuked them.

familiar.text: But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.

modern.text: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.

original.text: στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν ⸀αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: And they went to another village.

familiar.text: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.

modern.text: And He and His disciples went on to another village. The Cost of Discipleship (Matthew 8:18–22; Luke 14:25–33; John 6:59–66)

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς ἑτέραν κώμην.

verses.restored: As they were going on the way, someone said to him, I will follow you wherever you go.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, as they went in the way, a certain man said unto him, Lord, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

modern.text: As they were walking along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”

original.text: ⸀Καὶ πορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπέν τις πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ⸀ἐὰν ⸀ἀπέρχῃ.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Foxes have holes and birds of heaven nests, but the Son of Humanity has nowhere to lay the head.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.

verses.restored: He said to another, Follow me. But he said, Lord, permit me first to go away and bury my father.

familiar.text: And he said unto another, Follow me. But he said, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

modern.text: Then He said to another man, “Follow Me.” The man replied, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς ἕτερον· Ἀκολούθει μοι. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· ⸀Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ⸂ἀπελθόντι πρῶτον⸃ θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.

verses.restored: He said to him, Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but you, going away, proclaim the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: Jesus said unto him, Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.

modern.text: But Jesus told him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ⸀αὐτῷ· Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, σὺ δὲ ἀπελθὼν διάγγελλε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Another also said, I will follow you, Lord, but first permit me to say farewell to those in my house.

familiar.text: And another also said, Lord, I will follow thee; but let me first go bid them farewell, which are at home at my house.

modern.text: Still another said, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ ἕτερος· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι, κύριε· πρῶτον δὲ ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀποτάξασθαι τοῖς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, No one putting hand to plow and looking back is fit for the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

modern.text: Then Jesus declared, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Οὐδεὶς ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν ⸀χεῖρα ἐπʼ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω εὔθετός ἐστιν ⸂τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ τοῦ θεοῦ.
